New York City Has a Taste for Luxury, and the Name on Everyone's Lips Is the 2026 Lexus RX
14 photos
Photo: Eli Khalifa & SOS Auto Group/Facebook
New York City is arguably the worst place in America to own a car. Although it really depends on which borough you call home. If you’re in “the city”, meaning Manhattan, then you’re way better off using public transportation, as the vast majority of Manhattanites do. Besides, the cost of parking is on par with the GDP of a small African nation. Wakanda.
Yet, New Yorkers still buy cars, and expensive ones too. According to a report published by CarEdge , the most popular new vehicle in NYC for the past 45 days is the 2026 Lexus RX. And by most popular, I mean the best-selling car – 137 units sold over that time period.
To me, this comes as a surprise. Usually, it’ll be something like the Toyota RAV4, Honda CR-V or the Corolla. Not a Lexus. But as we’ve come to learn, the Japanese premium carmaker has magical powers when it comes to the U.S. market. You just utter the word Lexus and people think reliability, quality and resale value, the likes of which you’re not going to get with any of its German rivals.
I don’t necessarily agree, but perception is reality. This is as true in life as it is in the automotive industry.
Over the same 45-day period, the Lexus NX came fourth with 62 units sold, while the larger Lexus TX rounded out the top 5 with 54 units. That’s three Lexus models in the top 5, plus a Mercedes-Benz (GLE) at no.3.
To be fair, before we crown the RX the king of New York City , there’s an important distinction to be made here. CarEdge only looked at sales activity at dealerships associated with a particular location, and not all purchases made by NYC residents period. This is not a census of every vehicle sold to residents across all five boroughs.
Does this make the results any less intriguing? No way, Jose. I mean Johnny!
Five boroughs, Five New Yorks Manhattan is the home of the yellow cab, the Empire State Building, Chrysler Building, Central Park, and Madison Square Garden. Implicitly it’s the home of the New York Knicks and the New York Rangers. Brooklyn, on the other hand, is a proper cultural melting pot. A sort of mix between the Upper West Side of Manhattan and Queens. It’s also the home of the Brooklyn Nets. Nobody likes them.
Speaking of Queens, I think this might just be the most fascinating of the five boroughs for reasons I won’t go into right now. It’s the home of the New York Mets. Everyone likes them.
The Bronx? That’s where the Bombers live – aka the New York Yankees . As for Staten Island, it’s sort of a mix between NYC and New Jersey. By the way, the NFL’s NY Giants and Jets play across the Hudson river in New Jersey at Metlife Stadium, so they’re technically not in NYC.
Photo: Lexus Anyway, the point is that all five boroughs are different and the fact that different types of cars can be found topping borough-specific rankings makes perfect sense. For instance, Brooklyn’s best-selling new car in the aforementioned period? The 2026-27 Honda CR-V. In Queens? The 2026 Subaru Forester.
But it’s the Lexus RX that seems to occupy this particularly interesting middle ground. This is a premium SUV, or luxury SUV as some call it – although I wish people would stop saying that. Brands such as Mercedes, BMW, Audi and Lexus are not luxury brands. Rolls-Royce and Bentley are luxury brands. It’s pretty easy to make that distinction.
Long Island City: home of the Lexus RX This is where the most RX sales took place and that does make sense to me. Even though it’s technically a part of Queens, Long Island City has more in common with some of NYC’s more affluent neighborhoods as opposed to the suburban, Doug & Carrie, King of Queens-like image many Americans associate with Queens.
According to a report from the New York State Comptroller, Long Island City’s median household income was approximately $162,100 in 2023 – almost twice that of Sunnyside and Woodside.
But why the RX? Well, it’s large enough without being particularly cumbersome. It’s a proper mid-size SUV at 192.5 inches (4.9 m) in length, but you can maneuver it around way more easily than you would an Escalade or Navigator. And yet it still provides enough luggage space for a weekend getaway to the Hamptons (just watch out for ugly babies), to go with versatile powertrain choices.
The best choice being the RX 350h, which combines a naturally aspirated gasoline engine with an electric motor. This variant doesn’t require you to plug the car in, which is a major advantage in a city where having access to a dedicated parking space is already considered a major privilege – let alone one equipped with an EV charger.
Photo: Lexus Yes, a PHEV or BEV would be fantastic for someone with a wall charger at home. But if you often rely on commercial parking garages and/or street parking, the conventional hybrid is the way to go.
It’s also possible that New York City might not even “want” to own what some might consider the best luxury car. They might simply want the least complicated one. And this is true in Beverly Hills as well, another location where the Lexus RX recently came out on top, sales-wise. The RX; not the Range Rover , or the Cayenne or the Escalade.
How much is the RX? While the 2027 model year variant is already out, the 2026 RX is still for sale and the absolute cheapest one you can get is the RX 350 from $52,775. That’s the gasoline-powered front wheel drive variant. Meanwhile, the RX 350h AWD (the hybrid) starts from $55,075. Whether you think that’s a lot or a little, is entirely up to you.
All I’ll say is that the all-new 2027 BMW X5 starts from $72,110.
